name: shdr-27
title: SHDR-27
description: A weather-radar mosaic on the ball: the sphere is twisted by hashed vortices, each a rotation about the axis through it with a Gaussian falloff, and two scales of 3D noise are read through the twist and multiplied, so storm systems wind into spirals with concentric legend rings and drift on the clock. The dome is cut into a pixel grid that never rolls, each cell centre is inverse-projected onto the sphere and read once, so every dot is one flat colour from a seven-class radar legend — grey, blue, cyan, green, red, yellow, magenta — with the class boundaries dithered by a per-cell hash and the quiet areas thinned to a sparse twinkling scatter on cream paper.
